title: Okta Domain 4 questions (4.3 Authentication policies and network zones; 4.4 Password policies and self-service recovery)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with Okta.

questions.stem: An admin has added three rules to an app sign-in policy above the catch-all rule. How does Okta decide which rule governs a particular sign-in attempt?
choices: It applies the most restrictive rule whose conditions match
It merges the requirements of every rule whose conditions match
It applies the first rule in priority order whose conditions all match
It applies the rule that was created or edited most recently
questions.answer: It applies the first rule in priority order whose conditions all match
questions.explanation: Rules are evaluated top-down by priority and the first rule whose IF conditions all match is enforced. Okta does not merge or rank rules by strictness, so a broad rule placed high can hide a stricter one below it.

questions.stem: An admin creates a brand-new app sign-in policy and saves it without adding any rules. What does the policy contain?
choices: No rules at all, so every request to the assigned apps is denied
A catch-all rule that denies access until another rule is added
A catch-all rule that allows access with any two factor types
A copy of the rules in the global session policy
questions.answer: A catch-all rule that allows access with any two factor types
questions.explanation: Every new app sign-in policy starts with a single catch-all rule that allows access after any two factor types. Admins add their own rules above it; the policy is never empty and does not inherit global session policy rules.

questions.stem: Contractors must never reach the payroll app, while employees should get in after MFA. Both groups are assigned the app. What should the admin configure in the payroll app's sign-in policy?
choices: A Contractors rule with Access Denied, ranked above the employee rule
A change to the catch-all rule so that it excludes the Contractors group
A deny rule for the payroll app added inside the global session policy
A blocklist network zone that lists the Contractors group members
questions.answer: A Contractors rule with Access Denied, ranked above the employee rule
questions.explanation: A group-scoped rule with THEN Access is Denied, ranked above the allow rule, blocks contractors for that app only. The catch-all rule's conditions cannot be edited, and the global session policy is not scoped to individual apps.

questions.stem: Rule 1 in an app sign-in policy applies to the Finance group when User's IP is not in the Corporate zone. A Finance user opens the app from inside the office, which is in the Corporate zone. Which rule is enforced?
choices: The next matching rule in priority order, which may be the catch-all rule
Rule 1, because the user's group membership matches
No rule, so Okta denies access to the app
Only the global session policy, because no app sign-in rule matched
questions.answer: The next matching rule in priority order, which may be the catch-all rule
questions.explanation: All IF conditions of a rule must match. Because the network condition fails, Okta moves on to the next rule and ultimately the catch-all rule; it does not deny by default.

questions.stem: An app sign-in rule should apply to everyone assigned the app except the two members of a break-glass group. What is the BEST way to configure the rule?
choices: Create a second policy for the break-glass group with a lower priority
Exclude the break-glass group in the group membership condition
Add a custom expression that checks whether the user is active
Put the break-glass users' home IP addresses in an excluded network zone
questions.answer: Exclude the break-glass group in the group membership condition
questions.explanation: The group membership condition supports both include and exclude lists, so excluding the break-glass group keeps those accounts out of the rule. An app has only one sign-in policy, and IP-based exclusions are unreliable for identifying people.

questions.stem: An org created a Contractor user type and wants a rule that targets those accounts without maintaining a separate group. Which IF condition should the admin use?
choices: Device assurance policy is
User's IP is
User's user type is
Risk is
questions.answer: User's user type is
questions.explanation: The user type condition matches accounts by their Okta user type, so no group is needed. Device platform, network and risk conditions describe the request, not the kind of account.

questions.stem: Which app sign-in rule condition lets an admin add logic written in Okta Expression Language, such as a check on a user profile attribute?
choices: User's group membership includes
Device assurance policy is
The following custom expression is true
User is
questions.answer: The following custom expression is true
questions.explanation: The custom expression condition accepts Okta Expression Language, which can test profile attributes and other context. The other conditions are fixed pickers for groups, devices or named users.

questions.stem: A trading app must accept only possession factors that cryptographically verify the sign-in origin, so that a fake sign-in page cannot relay the challenge. Which rule setting should the admin choose?
choices: Authentication methods: Allow any method that can be used to meet the requirement
Prompt for authentication: Every time user signs in to resource
User must authenticate with: Any 1 factor type
Possession factor constraints are: Phishing-resistant
questions.answer: Possession factor constraints are: Phishing-resistant
questions.explanation: The phishing-resistant constraint only accepts authenticators that bind to the origin, such as Okta FastPass and passkeys. Prompting every time raises frequency, not resistance to relay attacks.

questions.stem: An app sign-in rule requires phishing-resistant possession factors. Which authenticators can users satisfy it with?
choices: Okta Verify push notifications and SMS one-time codes
Email magic links and answers to security questions
Google Authenticator codes and voice call codes
Okta FastPass and Passkey (FIDO2 WebAuthn)
questions.answer: Okta FastPass and Passkey (FIDO2 WebAuthn)
questions.explanation: Okta FastPass and FIDO2 WebAuthn passkeys verify the origin cryptographically. Push, one-time codes and email links can be relayed by a phishing proxy, so they do not meet the constraint.

questions.stem: HR wants users to verify again every time they open the HR app, even when they already have an active Okta session. Which change BEST meets this?
choices: Shorten the maximum session lifetime in the global session policy
Set the HR app rule to prompt every time the user signs in to the app
Turn on the option to stay signed in for the HR app rule
Add a Registered device state condition to the HR app rule
questions.answer: Set the HR app rule to prompt every time the user signs in to the app
questions.explanation: The re-authentication frequency in the app sign-in rule controls how often that one app prompts. Shortening the global session affects every app, and stay signed in reduces prompts rather than adding them.

questions.stem: The phone authenticator is enabled for the whole org, but the security team does not want SMS or voice accepted for one sensitive app. What should the admin do?
choices: Deactivate the phone authenticator under Security > Authenticators
Remove phone from the password policy's recovery options
Use Disallow specific authentication methods in that app's rule
Create a dynamic zone that excludes the mobile carrier networks' ASNs
questions.answer: Use Disallow specific authentication methods in that app's rule
questions.explanation: The Authentication methods setting in an app sign-in rule can disallow specific methods for just that app. Deactivating the authenticator would affect every user and app, and recovery settings do not control app access.

questions.stem: Which User must authenticate with option always requires the password, or the IdP that replaces it, plus one more distinct factor?
choices: Any 1 factor type
Password / IdP + Another factor
Possession factor
Password / IdP
questions.answer: Password / IdP + Another factor
questions.explanation: Password / IdP + Another factor demands the knowledge factor plus a second factor type. Any 2 factor types also gives MFA but does not insist on the password, and the remaining options are single-factor.

questions.stem: The global session policy asks only for a password. The finance app's sign-in policy requires any two factor types. A user signs in with a password and then opens the finance app. What happens?
choices: Okta grants access because a global session already exists for the user
Okta denies access because the two policies conflict
Okta ends the global session and restarts sign-in with two factors
Okta prompts for another factor before opening the finance app
questions.answer: Okta prompts for another factor before opening the finance app
questions.explanation: The app sign-in policy is evaluated when the app is accessed, and Okta steps the user up to meet its requirement. An existing global session does not satisfy a stricter app rule on its own.

questions.stem: Auditors require that users of a clinical app prove they are physically present with a PIN or biometric when they use Okta Verify. Which constraint settings should the admin select?
choices: Hardware protection alone, without requiring user interaction or verification
Device state is Registered
Any 1 factor type with no constraints
Require user interaction, then Require PIN or biometric user verification
questions.answer: Require user interaction, then Require PIN or biometric user verification
questions.explanation: Require user interaction ensures the user is present, and the PIN or biometric option adds user verification on top of it. Hardware protection only controls where keys are stored, and a registered device does not prove who is holding it.

questions.stem: Which possession factor constraint requires that authentication keys be stored in a TPM or Secure Enclave on the device?
choices: Phishing-resistant
Require user interaction
Device management is Managed
Hardware protection
questions.answer: Hardware protection
questions.explanation: Hardware protection checks that the keys live in secure hardware such as a TPM or Secure Enclave. Phishing resistance is about origin binding, which is a different property.

questions.stem: An admin needs to build a new policy that controls which authenticators users need to open a specific app. Where in the Okta Identity Engine Admin Console is this policy created?
choices: Security > Global Session Policy
Security > Networks
Security > Authentication Policies
Directory > Profile Editor
questions.answer: Security > Authentication Policies
questions.explanation: App sign-in (authentication) policies are created under Security > Authentication Policies and then applied to apps. The global session policy governs the Okta session, not individual apps.

questions.stem: An admin created a policy named High Assurance and wants a dozen finance apps to use exactly the same rules. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Add every finance app to the High Assurance policy
Clone the policy once for each app and keep the copies in sync
Add the finance apps to a rule in the global session policy
Assign the policy to the group that is assigned the apps
questions.answer: Add every finance app to the High Assurance policy
questions.explanation: One app sign-in policy can be shared by any number of apps, so changes are made once. Policies are applied to apps, not to groups, and the global session policy cannot target apps.

questions.stem: How many app sign-in policies are in effect for a single app integration at any one time?
choices: One for each group assigned to the app
Exactly one
Up to five, evaluated by priority
As many as needed, combined at runtime
questions.answer: Exactly one
questions.explanation: Each app is assigned one app sign-in policy; variations for different users are handled by rules within that policy. A policy, however, can be shared by many apps.

questions.stem: Management wants users to complete MFA before they can see the Okta End-User Dashboard itself. Which policy should the admin edit?
choices: The Default Policy password policy for all users
The Okta Dashboard app sign-in policy
The authenticator enrollment policy for all users
The Okta Admin Console app sign-in policy
questions.answer: The Okta Dashboard app sign-in policy
questions.explanation: The End-User Dashboard is a first-party app with its own app sign-in policy. The Admin Console policy only covers administrators opening the Admin Console, and password or enrollment policies do not control app access.

questions.stem: Every administrator must use phishing-resistant MFA to open the Admin Console, but ordinary users should not be affected. Which policy should the admin change?
choices: The default rule of the global session policy
The Okta Dashboard app sign-in policy
The authenticator enrollment policy for everyone
The Okta Admin Console app sign-in policy
questions.answer: The Okta Admin Console app sign-in policy
questions.explanation: The Okta Admin Console has its own app sign-in policy, so a stricter rule there affects only admin console access. Changing the global session policy or the Dashboard policy would affect all users.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes how the global session policy and an app sign-in policy work together in Okta Identity Engine?
choices: The app sign-in policy is evaluated first and can skip the global session policy
Only the stricter of the two policies is applied to each sign-in
The global session policy sets up the session; each app's policy is checked when it is opened
The global session policy covers only SAML apps; app policies cover only OIDC apps
questions.answer: The global session policy sets up the session; each app's policy is checked when it is opened
questions.explanation: Users must satisfy the global session policy to establish a session and then the app sign-in policy of each app they access. Both apply; neither replaces the other, and protocol does not decide which one is used.

questions.stem: An admin adds a new SAML app from the OIN and never selects a sign-in policy for it. Which policy controls access to the app?
choices: None; access is blocked until a policy is chosen
The preset Default Policy app sign-in policy
The Okta Dashboard app sign-in policy
The policy of the app that was added most recently
questions.answer: The preset Default Policy app sign-in policy
questions.explanation: New app integrations are assigned the preset Default Policy until the admin switches them to another app sign-in policy. Okta does not leave an app without a policy or borrow another app's policy.

questions.stem: An admin wants to define the company's office egress IP ranges so policies can treat office traffic differently. Where are these defined?
choices: Security > General
Settings > Account
Security > Authenticators
Security > Networks
questions.answer: Security > Networks
questions.explanation: Network zones, including IP zones and dynamic zones, are managed under Security > Networks. Security > General holds settings such as ThreatInsight, not zone definitions.

questions.stem: The office's public egress range is 203.0.113.0/24. Users in the office should skip extra prompts, while remote users must complete MFA. What should the admin do FIRST?
choices: Add that range to the trusted proxy IPs of a new zone
Create a dynamic zone for the office's country
Create an IP zone with that range as gateway IPs
Add that range to the ThreatInsight exempt zones
questions.answer: Create an IP zone with that range as gateway IPs
questions.explanation: Gateway IPs are the addresses Okta sees for the office, so an IP zone with that range lets rules test User's IP. Proxy IPs are for intermediaries in the forwarding chain, and a country is far too broad to represent one office.

questions.stem: All employee traffic passes through a cloud web proxy, so Okta sees the proxy's addresses instead of the real client IPs and zone rules stop matching. What should the admin configure?
choices: Add the proxy's addresses as gateway IPs in the existing Corporate zone
Create a dynamic zone with the IP type set to Any proxy and blocklist it
Add the proxy's addresses to a blocklist zone
Define the proxy's addresses as trusted proxy IPs in an IP zone
questions.answer: Define the proxy's addresses as trusted proxy IPs in an IP zone
questions.explanation: When an address is defined as a proxy, Okta walks the IP chain past it to find the real client IP. Listing the proxy as a gateway would make every proxied request look corporate, including those from home.

questions.stem: In which forms can an admin enter gateway addresses when creating an IP zone?
choices: Single IP addresses, CIDR ranges and IP address ranges
Host names and DNS domain names that resolve to the gateways
Country and region codes
Autonomous system numbers and internet service provider names
questions.answer: Single IP addresses, CIDR ranges and IP address ranges
questions.explanation: IP zones take individual addresses, CIDR blocks and start-end ranges. Locations and ASNs belong to dynamic zones, and host names are not accepted.

questions.stem: An admin has a Corporate IP zone and wants an app sign-in rule that requires MFA only when users are off the corporate network. How should the rule's User's IP condition be set?
choices: In any of the following zones, with only the Corporate zone selected
Anywhere, with Corporate listed as an exception in the policy
Blocklist, with Corporate selected as the blocked zone
Not in any of the following zones, with Corporate selected
questions.answer: Not in any of the following zones, with Corporate selected
questions.explanation: Not in any of the following zones matches requests from outside the selected zone, which is exactly the off-network case. Selecting In any of the following zones would do the opposite, and blocklisting the office would lock staff out.

questions.stem: A new branch office opens and its egress IP is added to the existing Corporate IP zone. Several rules already reference that zone. What else must the admin do for those rules to recognise the branch?
choices: Nothing; rules that reference the zone use its updated address list
Recreate each rule that references the zone so it reloads
Deactivate and reactivate each affected policy
Wait for the next directory import to sync the zone
questions.answer: Nothing; rules that reference the zone use its updated address list
questions.explanation: Rules reference the zone itself, so editing the zone's address list takes effect for every rule that uses it. That is the main benefit of defining zones once and reusing them.

questions.stem: Which criteria can an admin use to define a dynamic zone?
choices: Gateway IPs and trusted proxy IPs
Location, IP address type and ASN
Device platform and operating system version
User type and group membership
questions.answer: Location, IP address type and ASN
questions.explanation: Dynamic zones describe where traffic comes from by geolocation, proxy type and autonomous system number. Gateway and proxy lists define IP zones, and device or user attributes are policy conditions.

questions.stem: Security wants all requests from Tor exit nodes kept away from every page of the Okta org. What should the admin configure?
choices: A deny rule for Tor traffic in the Okta Dashboard app sign-in policy
A blocklisted dynamic zone with IP type Tor anonymizer proxy
Okta ThreatInsight set to log mode
A trusted proxy entry in an IP zone for the known Tor exit nodes
questions.answer: A blocklisted dynamic zone with IP type Tor anonymizer proxy
questions.explanation: A blocklisted dynamic zone with the Tor anonymizer IP type stops that traffic for the whole org. A Dashboard rule protects only one app, and log mode records threats without blocking them.

questions.stem: A request arrives from an IP address that is in a blocklist network zone. At what point does Okta stop it?
choices: After the global session policy but before the app sign-in policy
Only when an app sign-in rule references the zone
Before any policy evaluation takes place
After the user has entered a username and password
questions.answer: Before any policy evaluation takes place
questions.explanation: Blocklisted zones are enforced ahead of all policy evaluation, so the request never reaches sign-in. That makes blocklists suitable for known bad sources but risky for anything legitimate users might share.

questions.stem: Attacks keep arriving from many addresses that all belong to one hosting provider's network. What is the MOST efficient way to block the whole provider?
choices: Add the provider's ASN to a blocklisted dynamic zone
List each attacking address as a trusted proxy in an IP zone
Add a custom expression that checks for the provider's name
Add a rule that denies access when Risk is High
questions.answer: Add the provider's ASN to a blocklisted dynamic zone
questions.explanation: An ASN represents an entire network, so one entry covers every address the provider uses. Proxies are not blocks, and risk scoring may not flag every request.

questions.stem: An admin creates one dynamic zone with Location set to New Zealand and IP type set to Any proxy, then blocklists it, intending to block both proxies and New Zealand traffic. What will the zone actually block?
choices: Only requests that come from New Zealand through an anonymizing proxy
Every request that matches either condition
Nothing, because one dynamic zone cannot combine a location with an IP type
Only Tor requests, from any country
questions.answer: Only requests that come from New Zealand through an anonymizing proxy
questions.explanation: Conditions inside one dynamic zone are combined, so a request must match all of them. To block either condition separately, the admin needs two zones.

questions.stem: A policy currently denies access to an app for anyone whose IP geolocates outside the home country. Why should the admin avoid relying on location as the only control?
choices: Dynamic zones can only be used in password policy rules
Okta ignores network zones in rules that deny access
IP geolocation is approximate and traffic can be routed through VPNs
Dynamic zones stop matching once Okta has cached their locations
questions.answer: IP geolocation is approximate and traffic can be routed through VPNs
questions.explanation: IPs are dynamic and geolocation is approximate, so location should be one signal among several, combined with strong authentication. The other statements are not how network zones behave.

questions.stem: A regional app must only be reachable from the United States and Canada. Users elsewhere should be refused. Which configuration BEST meets this?
choices: A dynamic zone with both countries plus a deny rule for IPs outside it
An IP zone that lists both countries as gateway IPs
A blocklist dynamic zone that lists every country except the two allowed
A Device platform condition that is limited to North American devices only
questions.answer: A dynamic zone with both countries plus a deny rule for IPs outside it
questions.explanation: A dynamic zone captures countries, and a deny rule for requests outside it limits only that app. A blocklist would stop those countries from the entire org, and gateway lists accept addresses, not countries.

questions.stem: An app must only be reachable from devices that have been registered with Okta Verify. Which app sign-in rule condition should the admin set?
choices: Device platform is Windows or macOS
User's IP is in the Corporate zone
Device state is Registered
Risk is Low
questions.answer: Device state is Registered
questions.explanation: A registered device is one enrolled through Okta Verify, which is what the Device state condition checks. Platform and network conditions say nothing about whether the device is registered.

questions.stem: Security requires disk encryption and a minimum operating system version on laptops that open the finance app. What should the admin do?
choices: Create a device assurance policy and require it in the app rule
Set the Device platform condition to the newest operating system releases
Store each laptop's operating system version in a custom user attribute
Create a dynamic zone that contains company laptops
questions.answer: Create a device assurance policy and require it in the app rule
questions.explanation: Device assurance policies check posture such as OS version and disk encryption, and an app sign-in rule can require them for registered devices. Platform only checks the OS family, and zones describe networks rather than devices.

questions.stem: An app should only be opened from devices that are both registered with Okta Verify and managed by the company's device management solution. Which conditions should the rule use?
choices: Device state is Registered and Risk is Low
Device state is Registered and Device management is Managed
Device platform is iOS and User's IP is in the Corporate zone
Possession factor constraints are set to Hardware protection
questions.answer: Device state is Registered and Device management is Managed
questions.explanation: The Device management condition appears once Registered is chosen and limits the rule to managed devices. Risk, platform and hardware key storage do not prove the device is managed.

questions.stem: The security team wants any sign-in attempt that Okta scores as high risk to be refused for a sensitive app. Which rule should the admin add above the others?
choices: A rule with Device state Registered and Access set to Denied
A rule with User's IP Anywhere and two factor types
A rule with Device platform Any and Access set to Allowed
A rule with Risk is High and Access set to Denied
questions.answer: A rule with Risk is High and Access set to Denied
questions.explanation: The Risk condition matches attempts by Okta's risk level, so a top-priority deny rule for high risk blocks them. The other rules do not consider risk at all.

questions.stem: A credential-stuffing campaign is hitting the org from thousands of rotating IP addresses. The admin wants Okta to block requests from IPs it identifies as malicious before authentication. What should the admin configure?
choices: Set Okta ThreatInsight to log and enforce mode
Set Okta ThreatInsight to log mode only
Create an IP zone listing the attacking IPs as gateways
Raise the password lockout threshold in the password policy
questions.answer: Set Okta ThreatInsight to log and enforce mode
questions.explanation: ThreatInsight in enforce mode uses Okta's threat intelligence to block suspicious IPs before they reach authentication. Log mode only records the activity, and manual zones cannot keep up with rotating addresses.

questions.stem: The company's own load-testing service keeps being flagged by Okta ThreatInsight during scheduled tests. How should the admin stop this without weakening protection for everyone?
choices: Add the load-testing service's IP addresses to a blocklist network zone
Turn off Okta ThreatInsight for the org
Add the service's IPs to an allow rule in the global session policy
Add the service's network zone to the ThreatInsight exempt zones
questions.answer: Add the service's network zone to the ThreatInsight exempt zones
questions.explanation: ThreatInsight exempt zones exclude listed networks from its evaluation while keeping protection on for all other traffic. Blocking the service would break the tests, and disabling ThreatInsight removes protection entirely.

questions.stem: An admin wants a rule to apply only when users sign in from phones running iOS or Android. Which condition should the admin set?
choices: Device state is Registered
Device platform is, with iOS and Android selected
User's user type is
User's IP is not in the Corporate zone
questions.answer: Device platform is, with iOS and Android selected
questions.explanation: The Device platform condition matches the operating system of the request, so selecting iOS and Android scopes the rule to mobile platforms. Registration state and network do not identify the platform.

questions.stem: An admin wants an app rule to require MFA when Okta notices a user signing in from a location they have not used before. Which approach fits Okta Identity Engine?
choices: Reference a New Location behavior in the rule's custom expression
Create a dynamic zone of each user's past sign-in locations
Set Device state to Registered for all users
Add the country to the ThreatInsight exempt zones
questions.answer: Reference a New Location behavior in the rule's custom expression
questions.explanation: Behavior Detection tracks signals such as New Location, and app sign-in rules reference behaviors through Expression Language, for example security.behaviors.contains('New Location'). Per-user location zones are unworkable, and exempt zones reduce protection.

questions.stem: Where does an admin create and edit password policies in Okta Identity Engine?
choices: Security > Authentication Policies, then the Password tab
Security > General, under Password settings
Directory > People, then the password menu on a user's profile
Security > Authenticators, Password row, Actions > Edit
questions.answer: Security > Authenticators, Password row, Actions > Edit
questions.explanation: In Identity Engine, password policies belong to the password authenticator and are edited from its row under Security > Authenticators. Authentication policies control app access, not password rules.

questions.stem: A user belongs to two groups, and each group is assigned a different password policy. Which policy applies to the user?
choices: The policy with the strongest complexity settings
The highest-priority policy assigned to any of the user's groups
Both policies, with their settings combined
The Default Policy, because it always applies to everyone
questions.answer: The highest-priority policy assigned to any of the user's groups
questions.explanation: Password policies are evaluated in priority order, and the first one assigned to any of the user's groups wins. Okta does not merge policies or pick the strictest.

questions.stem: An admin built a stricter password policy for IT staff, but IT users still see the Default Policy requirements when they change passwords. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The Default Policy always overrides custom password policies
The policy isn't assigned to a group the IT users belong to
Password policies only apply to users created after the policy
The global session policy must also reference the new policy
questions.answer: The policy isn't assigned to a group the IT users belong to
questions.explanation: A password policy only applies to members of the groups it is assigned to; otherwise users fall through to the Default Policy. The Default Policy sits at the lowest priority, so it never overrides a matching custom policy.

questions.stem: Which statement about the Default Policy password policy is TRUE?
choices: It can be deleted once another password policy exists
It applies to everyone and always stays at the lowest priority
It applies only to users sourced from AD or LDAP
It is always evaluated before any custom policy
questions.answer: It applies to everyone and always stays at the lowest priority
questions.explanation: The Default Policy is the safety net that covers every user not matched by a higher policy, so it stays at the bottom and cannot be deleted. Custom policies are evaluated above it.

questions.stem: Employees and contractors share the same complexity rules, but only employees may use self-service password reset. What is the BEST configuration?
choices: A separate contractors password policy, ranked higher, with reset not allowed
Add a contractors exclusion to the global session policy
Create a Dashboard app sign-in policy that blocks the contractors
Change the contractors' user type to remove password reset
questions.answer: A separate contractors password policy, ranked higher, with reset not allowed
questions.explanation: Password policies are assigned to groups and ranked, so a separate contractor policy can carry its own self-service settings. Session and app sign-in policies do not decide who may reset a password.

questions.stem: Users are sourced from Active Directory and sign in with delegated authentication. Which system enforces the complexity rules for their passwords?
choices: The Okta Default Policy password policy for the org
The app sign-in policy assigned to the Okta Dashboard
The authenticator enrollment policy for the user's group
Active Directory, through its own password policy
questions.answer: Active Directory, through its own password policy
questions.explanation: With delegated authentication Okta checks credentials against AD, so AD's password policy enforces length, complexity and expiry. Okta still runs some checks, such as the common-password check, before sending a new password to AD, but it does not override AD's rules.

questions.stem: A security standard requires passwords of at least 12 characters and forbids well-known weak passwords such as Password123. Which password policy settings meet this?
choices: Minimum length 12 and Restrict use of common passwords
Password history of 12 passwords and a minimum age of 1 day
Lock out after 12 unsuccessful attempts
Password expires after 12 days with a reminder before expiry
questions.answer: Minimum length 12 and Restrict use of common passwords
questions.explanation: Minimum length and the common-password check are complexity settings that directly address the standard. History, age and lockout settings control reuse, rotation and guessing, not password strength.

questions.stem: Which complexity setting stops users from choosing a password that includes their own first name?
choices: Restrict use of common passwords
Enforce password history
Does not contain first name
At least one symbol
questions.answer: Does not contain first name
questions.explanation: The first name check compares the new password with the user's profile. The common-password list contains widely used passwords, not personal profile data.

questions.stem: An admin raises the minimum password length from 8 to 14 characters. What happens to users whose current passwords are only 10 characters long?
choices: Their status changes to Password expired immediately
They keep working; the new rule applies at the next password change
Their accounts are locked out until an admin unlocks them
Their passwords are reset and they receive a reset email
questions.answer: They keep working; the new rule applies at the next password change
questions.explanation: Complexity rules are checked when a password is set, so existing passwords are unaffected until they are changed. To force an immediate change, the admin would expire the passwords separately.

questions.stem: Which combination does Okta recommend as a baseline for password policies?
choices: No lockout, one-password history, no minimum age, six characters
Lockout, history, minimum age, eight or more characters, no common passwords
Expiry every 7 days with no history or minimum age
At least four characters with common passwords allowed
questions.answer: Lockout, history, minimum age, eight or more characters, no common passwords
questions.explanation: Okta's guidance is to combine lockout, history and minimum age with a minimum length of eight and the common-password check. The other options leave obvious gaps such as short passwords or no protection against guessing.

questions.stem: A user's new password Summer2026! meets every length and character requirement, yet Okta rejects it. Which setting MOST likely rejected it?
choices: Restrict use of common passwords
Minimum password age
Lock out after unsuccessful attempts
Password expiry reminder
questions.answer: Restrict use of common passwords
questions.explanation: Seasonal passwords like this appear on common-password lists, which Okta checks when the option is enabled. Minimum age and lockout do not evaluate the content of a new password.

questions.stem: Compliance asks that every password include an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number and a symbol. Where does the admin configure this?
choices: In the authenticator enrollment policy that covers the password authenticator
In a rule of the global session policy
In the complexity requirements of the applicable password policy
In the password attribute in Profile Editor
questions.answer: In the complexity requirements of the applicable password policy
questions.explanation: Character class requirements are part of the password policy's complexity settings. Enrollment policies decide which authenticators users must set up, not what a password must contain.

questions.stem: Users must not be able to reuse any of their last five passwords. Which password policy setting achieves this?
choices: Enforce password history for the last 5 passwords
Minimum password age of 5 days
Password expires after 5 days
Lock out after 5 unsuccessful attempts
questions.answer: Enforce password history for the last 5 passwords
questions.explanation: Password history keeps a record of previous passwords and rejects any of them. Minimum age and expiry control timing, and lockout counts failed sign-ins.

questions.stem: Auditors found users changing their password several times in one afternoon to cycle back to a favourite old password. Which setting BEST stops this?
choices: Lower the password expiry period
Lower the lockout threshold
Disable the common-password check
Set a minimum password age
questions.answer: Set a minimum password age
questions.explanation: A minimum age prevents rapid repeated changes, so users cannot flush the history list to reuse an old password. Shorter expiry would force even more changes and make the problem worse.

questions.stem: Policy requires passwords to expire every 90 days, with users warned two weeks ahead. Which settings should the admin configure?
choices: Minimum password age of 90 days and history of 14 passwords
Password expires after 90 days and prompt the user 14 days before expiry
Global session policy maximum session lifetime of 90 days
Lock out after 14 attempts and unlock after 90 minutes
questions.answer: Password expires after 90 days and prompt the user 14 days before expiry
questions.explanation: The password age section holds both the expiry period and the advance warning. Session lifetime controls how long a session lasts, not how long a password is valid.

questions.stem: A user's password reaches the end of its maximum age. What is the user's status, and what happens next?
choices: Locked out; an admin must unlock the account first
Suspended; the user cannot sign in until an admin reactivates the account
Deactivated; the account must be reactivated by an admin before sign-in
Password expired; the user must choose a new password at next sign-in
questions.answer: Password expired; the user must choose a new password at next sign-in
questions.explanation: An expired password puts the user in Password expired status, and Okta asks for a new password during the next sign-in. Locked out, Suspended and Deactivated come from other events and actions.

questions.stem: Following current NIST guidance, a company drops forced periodic password changes but still wants to prevent weak and reused passwords. What should the admin do?
choices: Turn off expiry but keep history and the common-password check
Turn off password history and keep expiry every 30 days
Set the minimum length to four characters and keep expiry every 90 days
Remove the password policy and rely on the Default Policy
questions.answer: Turn off expiry but keep history and the common-password check
questions.explanation: Modern guidance favours long, non-common passwords and history without arbitrary expiry. The Default Policy cannot be removed and is not a way to turn off settings.

questions.stem: A password policy prompts users several days before their password expires. What do users see during that window?
choices: An immediate lockout until they reset the password through the help desk
An email asking them to call the help desk before the password expires
A forced change with no option to continue
A reminder that it expires soon, with an option to change it now
questions.answer: A reminder that it expires soon, with an option to change it now
questions.explanation: The advance prompt warns users while their password is still valid and lets them change it early. A forced change only happens once the password has actually expired.

questions.stem: Accounts should lock after five failed sign-in attempts and unlock on their own after 30 minutes. Which settings should the admin configure in the password policy?
choices: Minimum password age of 5 hours and expiry after 30 days
Password history of 5 passwords and a reminder 30 days ahead
Lock out after 5 failed attempts; unlock automatically after 30 minutes
A 30-minute idle timeout in the global session policy rule
questions.answer: Lock out after 5 failed attempts; unlock automatically after 30 minutes
questions.explanation: Both the threshold and the automatic unlock time are in the password policy's lockout section. Session timeouts and password age settings do not count failed attempts.

questions.stem: Users who lock themselves out should be able to recover without calling the help desk by using a link on the Sign-In Widget. What should the admin enable?
choices: Unlock account in the password policy rule
Okta Verify push in the authenticator enrollment policy only
An app sign-in rule that allows locked-out users
A shorter session lifetime in the global session policy
questions.answer: Unlock account in the password policy rule
questions.explanation: The password policy rule's self-service options include Unlock account, which adds the Unlock account? link. Enrolling an authenticator alone does not turn the feature on.

questions.stem: A locked-out executive calls the help desk and needs access right away. What should the help desk admin do in the Admin Console?
choices: Open the user's profile and select Unlock
Reset the user's authenticators
Clear the user's sessions
Deactivate and then reactivate the user
questions.answer: Open the user's profile and select Unlock
questions.explanation: Unlock returns a Locked out user to Active without changing their password. Resetting authenticators or deactivating the user causes extra work and does not address the lockout directly.

questions.stem: A user exceeded the failed sign-in limit in the password policy. Which status does the Admin Console show for this user?
choices: Locked out
Password expired
Suspended
Password reset
questions.answer: Locked out
questions.explanation: Too many failed attempts move the user to Locked out. Password expired comes from age settings, Suspended from an admin action and Password reset from a reset in progress.

questions.stem: LDAP-sourced users are allowed to unlock their own accounts through self-service. What happens when one of them uses it?
choices: It is unlocked in both Okta and the LDAP directory
It is unlocked in Okta but stays locked in the LDAP directory
The account stays locked until the next LDAP import
The unlock fails because LDAP users cannot use self-service
questions.answer: It is unlocked in Okta but stays locked in the LDAP directory
questions.explanation: Self-service unlock only clears the Okta lockout for LDAP-sourced users; the lock in the on-premises directory remains. Admins must account for this when the directory enforces its own lockout.

questions.stem: An admin wants to see every account lockout in the past day in the System Log. Which filter is the BEST starting point?
choices: eventType eq "user.account.lock"
eventType eq "user.session.start"
eventType eq "user.lifecycle.deactivate"
eventType eq "user.account.update_password"
questions.answer: eventType eq "user.account.lock"
questions.explanation: The user.account.lock event records accounts that were locked after too many failed attempts. Session start, deactivation and password update events describe other activity.

questions.stem: In a password policy rule, which authenticators can a user choose to start self-service account recovery?
choices: Security question, password and temporary access code
Passkey, smart card and email
Okta Verify push, phone by SMS or voice, and email
Okta FastPass, security question and phone
questions.answer: Okta Verify push, phone by SMS or voice, and email
questions.explanation: The rule's recovery section lists Okta Verify push, phone and email, and also Google Authenticator, as ways to initiate recovery. Knowledge factors such as the password or a security question cannot start recovery; a security question can only serve as additional verification.

questions.stem: Users start password recovery with an emailed link, and the admin also wants them to answer a security question before setting the new password. Which rule setting should be used?
choices: Users can initiate recovery with: Security Question
Additional verification is: Only Security Question
Additional verification is: Not required
Possession factor constraints are: Require user interaction
questions.answer: Additional verification is: Only Security Question
questions.explanation: The additional verification setting adds a second check after the recovery authenticator, and Only Security Question limits it to that authenticator. Security questions cannot initiate recovery, and possession constraints belong to app sign-in rules.

questions.stem: An admin selects Phone as a recovery option, but many users never see it when they click Forgot password. Phone is optional in the authenticator enrollment policy. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Phone recovery only works for users covered by the Default Policy
Those users never enrolled a phone, since enrollment is optional
The global session policy blocks the phone authenticator during recovery
Phone recovery requires a dynamic network zone
questions.answer: Those users never enrolled a phone, since enrollment is optional
questions.explanation: Users can only recover with an authenticator they have enrolled, so optional enrollment leaves many without a phone. Okta recommends requiring the recovery authenticators in the enrollment policy.

questions.stem: An admin wants Okta Verify to be offered as a way to start password recovery, but the option cannot be used. Which prerequisite is MOST likely missing?
choices: Okta FastPass is not enabled for macOS devices
The password policy has no minimum password age configured yet
Okta Verify is not set as a gateway in the corporate network zone
Push is not enabled in the Okta Verify authenticator settings
questions.answer: Push is not enabled in the Okta Verify authenticator settings
questions.explanation: Okta Verify initiates recovery with a push notification, so push must be enabled on the Okta Verify authenticator. FastPass and password age are unrelated to recovery options.

questions.stem: An admin tries to enable Password reset in a password policy rule, but the rule does not allow users to change their password. What happens?
choices: Password reset works, but only through the help desk
Okta automatically allows password changes for the rule
Users can reset their password but cannot sign in to apps afterward
Reset can't be enabled until the rule allows password changes
questions.answer: Reset can't be enabled until the rule allows password changes
questions.explanation: Okta only permits self-service reset when the policy also allows password changes. The admin must allow changes first, then enable reset.

questions.stem: An admin wants to deactivate the phone authenticator, but Okta will not allow it. Phone is still listed as a recovery option in a password policy rule. What should the admin do FIRST?
choices: Delete every user's enrolled phone number in Directory > People
Remove phone from the password policy's recovery options
Move the password policy so it sits below the Default Policy
Turn off Okta ThreatInsight for the org before deactivating
questions.answer: Remove phone from the password policy's recovery options
questions.explanation: An authenticator that a password policy relies on for recovery must be removed from that policy before it can be disabled. Deleting enrollments or reordering policies does not remove the dependency.

questions.stem: Email is set to be used for recovery only, phone is enabled for authentication and recovery, and no other authenticators exist. Recovery starts with email or phone, and additional verification is Any enrolled authenticator used for MFA/SSO. Users who start with phone cannot finish. Why?
choices: Phone cannot start recovery when email is also enabled
Additional verification only accepts security questions in Identity Engine
Email is recovery-only, so no authenticator remains for the second check
Phone must be set for recovery only to start recovery
questions.answer: Email is recovery-only, so no authenticator remains for the second check
questions.explanation: After phone starts recovery, Okta needs a different authenticator used for MFA/SSO, and recovery-only email cannot fill that role. Requiring more authentication authenticators, or starting only with email, avoids the dead end.

questions.stem: The security team wants users to prove possession with an authenticator meeting a stronger standard before they can reset a password or unlock their account. Which approach does Okta Identity Engine provide?
choices: Add a rule to the Okta Dashboard app sign-in policy
Hand recovery access control to the Okta account management policy
Enable a stricter minimum password length
Set Additional verification to Not required in every password policy rule
questions.answer: Hand recovery access control to the Okta account management policy
questions.explanation: The Okta account management policy can govern recovery and unlock when the password policy rule hands access control to it. The Dashboard policy only controls opening the dashboard.

questions.stem: Where does an end user begin self-service password reset in Okta Identity Engine?
choices: The Okta Help Center support case form
The Applications tab of their profile in the End-User Dashboard
The Forgot password? link on the Okta Sign-In Widget
The Okta status page at status.okta.com
questions.answer: The Forgot password? link on the Okta Sign-In Widget
questions.explanation: Self-service reset starts from the Forgot password? link on the Sign-In Widget, followed by verification with a recovery authenticator. Support resources and status pages are not part of the recovery flow.

questions.stem: A user forgot their password and has not enrolled any recovery authenticator. What should the help desk do so the user can set a new password?
choices: Clear the user's sessions
Reset the user's authenticators
Reset password on the user's profile to send a reset link
Suspend the user and then unsuspend them to refresh the account
questions.answer: Reset password on the user's profile to send a reset link
questions.explanation: An admin-initiated reset sends the user a link to set a new password without needing a recovery authenticator. Clearing sessions or resetting authenticators does not give the user a new password.

questions.stem: After a phishing report, security wants a user to sign in once more with their current password and then be forced to choose a new one. Which action fits?
choices: Expire password
Reset password
Unlock
Reset authenticators
questions.answer: Expire password
questions.explanation: Expire password keeps the current password valid for one sign-in and then requires a change. Reset password invalidates the current password and sends a reset link instead.

questions.stem: An admin clicked Reset password for a user, and the user has not yet clicked the reset link. Which status does the user's profile show?
choices: Password expired
Locked out
Staged
Password reset
questions.answer: Password reset
questions.explanation: A reset in progress shows the Password reset status until the user completes it. Password expired results from expiry or the Expire password action, and Staged users have never been activated.

questions.stem: A user's credentials were stolen. The admin has reset the password, but the attacker may still hold an active Okta session. What should the admin do next?
choices: Expire the user's password
Unlock the user
Move the user to a new password policy
Clear the user's sessions
questions.answer: Clear the user's sessions
questions.explanation: Clearing the user's sessions signs out any session the attacker already holds, so it should follow a credential compromise rather than relying on the password reset alone. Expiring the password or changing policy does not end an existing session.

questions.stem: An Active Directory-sourced user with delegated authentication completes self-service password reset in Okta. What happens to their password?
choices: The new password is stored only in Okta, and AD keeps the old password
The reset fails because AD users cannot reset in Okta
Okta sends the new password to Active Directory through the AD agent
Okta disables delegated authentication for that user
questions.answer: Okta sends the new password to Active Directory through the AD agent
questions.explanation: With delegated authentication the AD agent writes the new password to AD, which stays the source of truth. The user then signs in to Okta and AD-joined resources with the same new password.

questions.stem: The help desk needs to reset passwords and unlock accounts but must not change policies or apps. Which standard admin role BEST fits?
choices: Read-only Administrator
Report Administrator
Help Desk Administrator
Application Administrator
questions.answer: Help Desk Administrator
questions.explanation: The Help Desk Administrator role can reset passwords and unlock users without broader configuration rights. Read-only and Report admins cannot take these actions, and Application admins manage apps.

questions.stem: An admin must require MFA for the expense app only when users are off the corporate network. Put the steps in order.
items: In Security > Networks, create an IP zone with the office gateway IPs
In Security > Authentication Policies, create an app sign-in policy with a rule where User's IP is not in the corporate zone that requires two factor types
Add the expense app to the new policy
Sign in from outside the office and confirm that Okta asks for a second factor
questions.explanation: The zone must exist before a rule can reference it, the rule lives in a policy, and the policy only takes effect once the app is assigned to it. Testing from outside the zone verifies the requirement.

questions.stem: Match each app sign-in rule setting to what it does.

pairs.match: Accepts only factors that verify the sign-in origin
Requires keys kept in a TPM or Secure Enclave
Requires the user to be physically present
Removes chosen methods for this app only
Blocks users who match the rule's conditions

targets_extra: Blocks the request before any policy runs
questions.explanation: These are the THEN settings of an app sign-in rule. Blocking a request before any policy runs is what a blocklist network zone does, not a rule setting.

questions.stem: An admin is creating a dynamic zone rather than an IP zone. Which TWO criteria can the admin use to define it?
choices: Location such as a country or region
Autonomous system number of the network
Gateway IP addresses in CIDR form
Device platform of the request
User type of the account
answers: Location such as a country or region
Autonomous system number of the network
questions.explanation: Dynamic zones are defined by location, IP type and ASN. Gateway addresses define IP zones, and device platform and user type are app sign-in rule conditions.

questions.stem: An admin wants users to reset forgotten passwords with an email link followed by a security question. Put the steps in order.
items: In Security > Authenticators, add and enable the Security Question authenticator
Open the Password row and choose Actions > Edit
Edit the rule of the policy assigned to the users' group
Allow password reset, select Email for recovery and set additional verification to Only Security Question
Test with the Forgot password? link on the Sign-In Widget
questions.explanation: The security question must be available as an authenticator before a password policy rule can require it. Recovery is configured in the password policy rule and verified through the Forgot password? flow.

questions.stem: Match each password policy setting to the problem it addresses.

pairs.match: Users cycle through changes to get back an old password
Users pick widely known weak passwords
Users are surprised when a password expires

targets_extra: Users keep an active session on a shared computer
questions.explanation: Each setting targets one weakness in password handling. Sessions left open on shared computers are handled by the global session policy and by clearing sessions, not by a password setting.

questions.stem: An admin is choosing which authenticators may start self-service password recovery in a password policy rule. Which TWO can be selected?
choices: Email
Okta Verify with push
Security question
Okta FastPass
Password
questions.explanation: Recovery can be started with Okta Verify push, phone, email or Google Authenticator. A security question can only be added as additional verification, and Okta FastPass and the password itself do not start recovery.
